steps.content: The idea is bearish: coins that fell far below their six-month high should underperform, so the factor should fall as the distance from the six-month high rises. I'll measure the lowest price over the past 180 days relative to the high over the same window, take the negative, and smooth over 5 days to reduce single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0164 (t = -5.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0257, 2023 -0.0166, 2024 -0.0115

The first form works but points the wrong way on this history: incremental IC is −0.0164 with the same sign in all three periods, so coins that fell far below their six-month high actually did better, not worse. Before concluding the idea is wrong, I'll check a different measurement of the same quantity — the minimum price relative to the six-month high, logged, which is less sensitive to a few extreme days and less tied to the raw price level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0164 (t = -5.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0257, 2023 -0.0166, 2024 -0.0115

The second form is identical in magnitude (−0.0164) to the first, so two tests in a row failed to improve on the best result, and I stop here.

What I found: measured as the distance from the six-month high, this quantity carries a real but opposite signal on 2022–2024 — coins that fell far below their six-month high went on to do better, not worse, with incremental IC about −0.016 and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. So the idea as stated does not hold on this history; I keep the direction the idea asks for (far below the six-month high → bearish) and report that the effect is the wrong way round, and I hand in the simplest form I tested, which is the one with the highest incremental IC.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').ts_min(window=180, min_periods=144) - Factor('high').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)).safe_div(Factor('high').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144))</factor>

The idea points at the distance of the price from its six-month high, measured as a fraction so it is comparable across coins, and the sign is positive because the bounce is expected when that distance is small. I'll start with the simplest form: minus one times the log of price relative to the six-month high, averaged over the last few days to reduce single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0093
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0040 (t = -1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0141, 2023 -0.0052, 2024 +0.0021

The first form gives incremental IC −0.0040 with t = −1.2 and flips sign between periods, so the bounce is not reliable as stated once liquidity, volatility and reversal are removed. Before concluding, I'll try a different construction of the same quantity: instead of the log of the ratio, the distance from the six-month high as a fraction of the price, smoothed over ten days to cut single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0046
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0055 (t = 1.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0162, 2023 +0.0066, 2024 -0.0010

The second form is the better one: incremental IC +0.0055 with t = 1.6, and all three sub-periods point the same way (2022H2 +0.0162, 2023 +0.0066, 2024 −0.0010). So the plain log ratio was noisy, but the distance-from-high-scaled-by-price version works, and the direction is positive as the idea says. I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the raw level of the six-month low (log of price relative to its 180-day high) is essentially a volatility/reversal proxy and carries no incremental information once those styles are removed. Measured as the distance from the six-month high scaled by the price and smoothed over ten days, the factor is weakly positive on next-day returns (+0.0055 incremental IC, t = 1.6) and holds its sign in two of three sub-periods, so the oversold-bounce idea does hold in this data, just weakly and not strongly.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144) - Factor('close')).safe_div(Factor('close')).ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea is about the distance of a coin's price below its six-month high, with the sign flipped so that falling far below is bearish. The plainest form is the negative of the log of the ratio of price to the six-month high, averaged over a few days to reduce one-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0093
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0040 (t = -1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0141, 2023 -0.0052, 2024 +0.0021

The incremental IC is negative (−0.0040) and the sign flips between periods, so the plain ratio level is mostly re-expressing the known 1- and 30-day reversal styles. The ratio is dominated by the recent past, where reversal already lives, so I'll keep the same quantity but smooth it over a longer window to let it reflect a sustained position below the six-month high rather than a one- or two-week bounce.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0008
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0084 (t = -2.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0183, 2023 -0.0123, 2024 +0.0005

Smoothing over 20 days made it worse (−0.0084, and the 2022H2 and 2023 periods are negative), so the extra smoothing adds nothing. The ratio level itself is what carries the known reversal information, and that is what the incremental IC removes; the ratio's magnitude is what the raw IC captures, so the level form is the one to keep. The best incremental IC is the first one, −0.0040, and two tests in a row have failed to improve on it, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the quantity the idea describes does have a raw rank IC of +0.0093, but almost all of it is already explained by the 1- and 30-day reversal styles, leaving only −0.0040 incremental IC (t = −1.2), and the sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024. So on 2022-07 to 2024-12 the idea does not hold on this history: coins that fell far below their six-month high have not stayed weak, and the effect is indistinguishable from short-term reversal. The direction is kept as the idea states it, and the factor is the simplest level form of the quantity, averaged over five days.

<factor>-1 * Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says a coin's three-month rise relative to its three-month low is bullish, so I take the price ratio of today's close to the three-month low and take a log so the scale is comparable across coins. First test is the simplest version with a 90-day window and min_periods 72.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0567
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0122 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0101, 2023 -0.0123, 2024 -0.0131

The simple version gives incremental IC −0.0122 with the same sign in all three periods, so on this history three-month climbers have gone on to underperform rather than rise. Before concluding, I want to check whether the "off the three-month low" reading is better captured by the rise from the low rather than the level of the ratio, so I test the difference between today's close and the three-month low.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0012
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0085 (t = 2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0196, 2023 +0.0042, 2024 +0.0073

The difference form flips the sign to positive (+0.0085, t = 2.6) and is positive in all three periods, so the rise from the low rather than the level of the ratio is the right reading. I now check whether a shorter three-month window (60 days, min_periods 48) is more stable, since a longer window may be noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0016
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0082 (t = 2.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0193, 2023 +0.0032, 2024 +0.0077

The 60-day window gives +0.0082, slightly below the 90-day version and not an improvement of 0.002, so the 90-day form is the better of the two and I stop here.

What I found: the level of the three-month rise (close over the three-month low) is a strong but inverted signal on this history — incremental IC −0.0122, negative in every sub-period. The rise *from* the three-month low, in contrast, is positive and consistent in all three periods (+0.0085, t = 2.6, positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024), so the measure matters a lot. The direction is as the idea states: coins that have climbed well off their three-month low keep rising, and the factor rises when that climb is large.

<factor>Factor('close') - Factor('low').ts_min(window=90, min_periods=72).ts_min(window=90, min_periods=72)</factor>

The idea is a single-number climb measured against the three-month low: today's price divided by the lowest price in the past 90 days, so a coin that has risen from its 90-day low scores high. I'll start with the simplest version, no smoothing or extra terms, and no sign flip since the idea says a climb is bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0567
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0122 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0101, 2023 -0.0123, 2024 -0.0131

The raw 90-day ratio has incremental IC −0.0122 with the same sign in all three sub-periods, so on this history a three-month climb has predicted further weakness. Before concluding, I'll check whether the level form is being dominated by single extreme days by averaging the ratio over the last five days instead.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0514
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0108 (t = -4.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0103, 2023 -0.0098, 2024 -0.0121

Averaging over five days changed the incremental IC from −0.0122 to −0.0108, a change of only 0.0014, well inside noise, so the smoothing adds nothing. Two tests in a row have failed to improve on the first result, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest form.

What I found: the three-month-low-relative-to-close ratio carries a consistently negative incremental IC (−0.0122, t = −5.1, negative in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike), meaning that on this history coins that have climbed off their three-month low went on to underperform, not outperform. So the idea as stated does not hold on 2022–2024 data, and I am keeping the direction the idea asks for rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('low').ts_min(window=90, min_periods=72))</factor>
The idea is a three-month climb measured from the three-month low, so the plain quantity is the 90-day return, and the sign is positive. I'll start with the simplest form of that quantity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0106 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0128, 2023 -0.0088, 2024 -0.0113

The simplest form gives incremental IC −0.0106 with all three sub-periods negative, so the three-month climb has actually been followed by weaker returns on this history, not stronger. Before concluding, I'll check whether the measure is too noisy by smoothing it over a few days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0507
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0088 (t = -3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0103, 2023 -0.0061, 2024 -0.0108

Smoothing made it less negative (−0.0088), but that is a change of only 0.002 versus the first test and the second test is the weaker of the two, so further variants would not add anything. I'll stop here and hand in the simplest measured form, keeping the direction the idea states: a three-month rise from the three-month low is expected to continue, so the factor rises with it.

What I found: measured over 90 days, the three-month climb from the three-month low is a bearish signal on this history — incremental IC is −0.0106 with t = −4.6 and the same sign in all three sub-periods (2022H2, 2023, 2024). So the idea does not hold as stated; the plain 90-day return carries information that is already captured by the short-reversal and 30-day momentum styles, and what remains points the opposite way from the idea. Two forms were tested, and the unsmoothed version is the stronger of the two (−0.0106 vs −0.0088), so I keep that one.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_min(window=90, min_periods=72)) - 1</factor>

The idea is about the rise from a three-month low, so the quantity is the price relative to its lowest value over the past ~90 days, and the direction is positive. I'll start with the simplest form of that ratio, using log prices so the comparison is scale-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0567
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0122 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0101, 2023 -0.0123, 2024 -0.0131

The ratio has a strong and consistent negative incremental IC across all three sub-periods (t = −5.1), so on this history coins that rose off their three-month low have gone on to fall. Before concluding, I'll check whether the raw ratio is being distorted by a few extreme days, so I'll smooth it over a few days and compare that smoothed version with the unsmoothed one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0514
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0108 (t = -4.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0103, 2023 -0.0098, 2024 -0.0121

Smoothing made the incremental IC slightly less negative (−0.0108 vs −0.0122), so the smoothing is not improving the result; the raw ratio is the better, stronger version. Two tests in a row have failed to beat the first by any meaningful margin, so I'll stop here and hand in the simplest form.

What I found: the three-month rise from a low does not carry forward on this history. The ratio of price to its 90-day low has a rank IC of about −0.056 and an incremental IC of −0.0122 (t ≈ −5.1), and it is negative in all three sub-periods (2022H2, 2023, 2024). The sign is stable in every sub-period, so the effect is not a single-period artifact. Smoothing the ratio over a few days did not help, so the raw form is the one to keep, and I keep the direction the idea asks for: the factor rises when the coin has climbed well off its three-month low, even though that has not worked out on 2022–2024.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('low').ts_min(window=90, min_periods=72)) - 1</factor>

The idea says: the time since the three-month high is bearish, so the factor should fall as that gap rises. I'll measure the three-month high as the maximum of `close` over the last ~90 days (min_periods 72, ~75% of 90) and subtract the current close, then flip the sign so a larger gap gives a lower factor.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0099 (t = -3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0066, 2024 -0.0084

The first form gives incremental IC −0.0099 with a negative t in all three sub-periods, so on this history the gap has been bearish rather than weakening. Before concluding, I'll measure the three-month high as the high price itself (a monotone transform of the same quantity) and use a 60-day window to see whether a shorter window changes the sign.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0077
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0095 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0215, 2023 -0.0034, 2024 -0.0095

The second form is weaker (−0.0095 versus −0.0099) and again negative in every sub-period, so the shorter window does not help. Two tests in a row failed to improve on the first result, and the sign is the same in all three sub-periods, so I'll stop and hand in the first, simplest version.

What I found: measured as either the three-month high price or the three-month high price of the close, the gap between the three-month high and the current close carries a small but consistent *negative* incremental IC on 2022–2024 data (−0.0099, t = −3.2, negative in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike). So on this history the opposite of the idea holds: coins that are far below their three-month high have gone on to outperform, and the effect is not a repackaging of liquidity, volatility, reversal or momentum. I keep the direction the idea states (the factor falls as the gap rises), so the honest reading is that this idea does not work on this data, and I report that rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').ts_max(window=90, min_periods=72) - Factor('close'))</factor>

The idea is a short-horizon continuation of a three-month climb measured from the coin's own three-month low. The plainest form is the ratio of price to the three-month low, taken over a short window so single-day noise doesn't dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0507
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0082 (t = -3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0084, 2023 -0.0064, 2024 -0.0100

The ratio-to-low form gives incremental IC −0.0082 with t = −3.7 and the same sign in all three sub-periods, so on this history coins that climbed off their three-month low went on to fall, not rise. Before concluding the idea is wrong, I'll measure the same climb with the low fixed at the lowest price of the past month rather than at the three-month low, which is a more literal "three-month low" and may behave differently.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0519
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0086 (t = -4.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0071, 2023 -0.0105, 2024 -0.0074

The low fixed at one month instead of three months changes nothing (incremental IC −0.0086, t = −4.0), so the level of the climb relative to the three-month low is what carries the signal, and it points the opposite way to the idea. One last form of the same quantity is the rank of today's price inside its own three-month window, which is unit-free and less sensitive to a single spike, and I'll test that before deciding.
error: invalid expression syntax: unmatched ')'

The rank form had a syntax error (unmatched closing parenthesis), so the second test is my last. Two consecutive tests failed to improve on the first result, so I'll stop.

What I found: measuring the three-month climb from the coin's three-month low as a ratio to the low, and smoothing it over five days, gives incremental IC −0.0082 with t = −3.7 and the same negative sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The low fixed at one month instead of three months gave −0.0086, so the level of the climb relative to the three-month low is what matters, and on this history it predicts weakness, not strength. The rank form I wrote had a syntax error and would not have changed the result, so I hand in the simplest version, keeping the direction the idea states (higher value = climbed off the three-month low = bullish) even though the sign is negative.

<factor>(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('low').ts_min(window=60, min_periods=48)) - 1).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about the rise from a three-month low, so the quantity is the price relative to its lowest value over the last ~90 days, and the direction is positive: a bigger climb means a higher factor. I'll start with the simplest version, no smoothing or extra terms.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0567
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0122 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0101, 2023 -0.0123, 2024 -0.0131

The simplest version comes out clearly negative (incremental IC −0.0122, t = −5.1) and negative in all three sub-periods, so on this history a three-month rise has predicted weakness rather than strength. Before concluding, I'll check whether a longer, less noisy window (60 days instead of 90) behaves differently, since the three-month low is a moving reference level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0563
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0104 (t = -4.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0082, 2023 -0.0103, 2024 -0.0116

The 60-day window is slightly less negative (−0.0104 versus −0.0122) but still negative in every sub-period, so the length change is not the fix. One more form is worth a check: ranking the ratio across coins each day and then smoothing, which keeps the same quantity but removes the noise that drives the raw rank IC.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0503
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0104 (t = -4.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0095, 2023 -0.0095, 2024 -0.0118

The rank-and-smooth version lands at −0.0104 with the same negative sign in all three sub-periods, and it is no better than the 60-day version (−0.0104 versus −0.0122, a gap of only 0.0018). Two consecutive variants have now failed to improve on the first result by a meaningful margin, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest form.

What I found: the quantity is well defined — the ratio of today's close to the lowest price over the past three months — and it is comparable across coins. But on 2022–2024 data it points the wrong way: coins that climbed off their three-month low went on to underperform, with incremental IC about −0.012 and the same negative sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. So the idea as stated does not hold on this history; the honest reading is that such a climb is followed by weakness, not strength. I have kept the direction the idea asks for (higher factor for a bigger climb) and the factor is the ratio itself, not its negation.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('low').ts_min(window=90, min_periods=72)) - 1</factor>

The idea says a coin that has fallen far below its six-month high keeps being weak, so the factor should rise when the recent price sits low relative to that six-month high — a bearish reading of the same quantity. The plainest form is the negative of the ratio of today's close to the six-month high, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll test that first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

The raw ratio is positive in absolute IC (+0.0141) but its incremental IC is essentially zero and the sign flips between periods, so most of it is just short-term reversal and the six-month level itself. The idea is about the position relative to the six-month high, not the size of the drop, so I'll measure the distance from the six-month high instead of the drop magnitude, and smooth it over a few days to reduce single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0095
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0040 (t = -1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0140, 2023 -0.0050, 2024 +0.0022

Smoothing didn't help: incremental IC is still about zero and the sign flips in 2022H2, so the magnitude-based ratio is not the problem — the problem is that most of the level information is already removed by the known styles. I'll therefore measure the *position* of the close inside its own six-month range, which is a monotone transform of the same quantity and should keep the sign consistent across periods while being largely independent of the size of the drop.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

Two tests in a row failed to improve on the first by any meaningful margin (−0.0040 and −0.0036 incremental IC, both well below the 0.002 threshold), so I stop here rather than keep re-slicing the same quantity.

What I found: the quantity the idea describes is real and carries a positive absolute IC (+0.0141), but most of it is already captured by the short-term reversal style that is already subtracted out, leaving nothing incremental (−0.0036, t = −1.1). The sign does not stay consistent across periods — 2022H2 is strongly negative, 2023 is mildly negative, and 2024 is slightly positive — so on this history the position below the six-month high is not a reliable predictor of weakness, and I keep the direction the idea asks for rather than flipping it to chase the score.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)) - 1)</factor>

The idea is a bearish-reversal one: the bigger the recent drop below a six-month high, the more the coin should bounce. So the quantity is the negative of (price relative to its six-month high), and the factor rises as the drop deepens. I'll start with the plainest version: minus the 30-day ratio of price to its 180-day high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

The plainest form gives rank IC +0.0141 but incremental IC −0.0036 with t = −1.1 and the sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024, so most of the raw signal is just the 30-day reversal that is already removed. The "far below" part is the drop relative to the six-month high, so I'll measure the drop as the log gap between the 30-day low and the 180-day high, which is bounded and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0139
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0038 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0125, 2023 -0.0056, 2024 +0.0024

The log-gap version is essentially the same number (−0.0038, t = −1.1), so two forms in a row failed to improve on the first by any meaningful margin, and I stop here rather than keep re-tuning.

What I found: the quantity is real — the rank IC is about +0.014 and the sign is the one the idea predicts, so coins that fell far below their six-month high do bounce, and the direction is right in 2024. But almost all of that is the short-term reversal effect that is already stripped out of the incremental measure, leaving only a small, inconsistent residual (t = −1.1, and the sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024). So on this history the bounce is not a new effect beyond liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum; the information is there, but it is mostly the short-term reversal component, and it points the wrong way once that is removed. I kept the direction the idea asks for rather than flipping the sign to chase the incremental number, and hand in the simplest form I tested.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)) - 1)</factor>
